name: Serbia

income_tax.summary: Flat 10% salary tax with a monthly non-taxable amount (about RSD 25,000 per CountryTaxCalc; not applied here), plus employee contributions of 19.9% (self-employed entrepreneurs pay 35.05%) (14% pension, 5.15% health, 0.75% unemployment). A supplementary annual personal income tax of 10% above three times the average annual salary and a further rate above six times applies to high earners (thresholds not given in RSD).
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Entrepreneurs (preduzetnici) pay the full contribution themselves at the Article 44(1) rates of the Law on Mandatory Social Insurance Contributions: pension 24% + health 10.3% + unemployment 0.75% = 35.05% of the contribution base (the base is the entrepreneur's own salary, or taxable profit if none, or the lump-sum amount under paušal; Article 22), subject to a minimum and a maximum base (five times the average monthly salary; the RSD amounts were not found, so the cap is left null). Entrepreneurs doing work with enhanced service credit pay a further 3.7-11%. At about EUR 54k (roughly RSD 6.3 million, assuming ~117 RSD/EUR, an assumption) turnover exceeds the RSD 6,000,000 paušal ceiling (Income Tax Law, Art. 40), so the 35.05% on actual profit applies; the paušal option (about RSD 30,000-60,000 a month combined tax and contributions per CountryTaxCalc, an unofficial figure) is not available above that turnover. Income tax on self-employment income is 10% (Art. 38).
income_tax.local_tax_note: Contribution base for employees is between 35.05% and five times the average monthly salary (RSD amounts not found), so the cap is left null. The Income Tax Law page opened shows a monthly non-taxable amount of RSD 37,369 for full-time earnings (indexed yearly; version and 2026 value not confirmed) whereas CountryTaxCalc says about RSD 25,000; neither is applied (effect under ~EUR 400 a year).

Self-employed 35.05% is the statutory rate; minimum/maximum bases in RSD not found, so the effective rate at low or very high incomes may differ.
Employee total is 19.9% on PwC (with unemployment); CountryTaxCalc says 19.15%.

regimes.name: Temporary residence for remote workers (reported)
regimes.description: Third-party summaries (WFA) describe a temporary residence permit for people working for foreign employers or clients, with income of at least USD 42,000 a year, health insurance and funds, valid up to one year and renewable. CountryTaxCalc says Serbia has no official digital nomad visa as of mid-2026 and that the temporary-residence permit does not itself grant work authorization. Legal hook: Article 40(4) of the Law on Foreigners lets the Government define categories of foreigners for temporary residence by a separate act, and its example list includes 'stranci digitalni nomadi'; the implementing act and its income test were not found, so the USD 42,000 figure is unconfirmed. No tax change: Serbian tax residency after 183 days (WFA).
regimes.duration_note: Reported as one year, renewable (a 2026 guide not opened says three years).

open_questions: The Law on Foreigners (Art. 40(4)) names digital nomads as a category the Government may define, but the implementing act was not found; income threshold USD 42,000 rests on WFA only.
Social-security treatment of a foreign-paid worker is stated only by WFA.

residence_routes: EU, US and many other citizens can enter visa-free for 90 days; longer stays need a temporary residence permit (initially one year, renewable) with a lease, funds, health insurance and criminal record (CountryTaxCalc). Working normally needs entrepreneur registration or a work permit. Permanent residence after five years. Serbia is not in the EU or Schengen.
open_questions: Nomad route: legal basis exists (Law on Foreigners Art. 40(4)) but operating criteria, fees and income test unverified on an official page.
